aiOverview.content: Travel vaccines are immunizations recommended or required for international travel to protect against diseases not commonly found in the United States, such as yellow fever, typhoid, and Japanese encephalitis. It is highly recommended to consult a healthcare provider or travel specialist 4–6 weeks before departure to allow time for vaccines to take effect and to complete multi-dose series. Commonly Recommended Travel Vaccines Hepatitis A: Recommended for most travelers to countries where the disease is common. Typhoid: Recommended for travelers visiting smaller cities, villages, and rural areas, particularly in South Asia. Yellow Fever: Required for entry into certain countries in Africa and South America, often requiring an International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP). Japanese Encephalitis: Recommended for travelers planning a month or longer in endemic areas in Asia, or short-term travelers visiting rural areas. Rabies: Recommended for travelers going to remote areas, animal handlers, or those staying for long periods in countries where rabies is common. Meningococcal Disease: Required for travelers going to Saudi Arabia for Hajj/Umrah, and recommended for the "meningitis belt" of Africa. Tick-borne Encephalitis (TBE): Recommended for travelers to endemic areas in Europe and Asia who will be hiking, camping, or spending time outdoors. Routine Vaccines (Ensure You Are Up-to-Date) Many travelers may need boosters for routine vaccines, which are crucial due to outbreaks in other countries: Measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) Tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap) COVID-19 Polio: A polio booster is currently recommended for adults traveling to over 30 countries with recent poliovirus detections. Influenza (Flu) Key Considerations Last-Minute Travel: Even if travel is soon, a consultation is valuable. Some vaccines can be given on an accelerated schedule. Yellow Fever Waiver: If the yellow fever vaccine is contraindicated, a medical waiver can be issued. Proof of Vaccination: Some countries require a stamped ICVP for entry, valid 10 days after the yellow fever vaccine is administered. Where to Go: Travel vaccines may not be available at all primary care offices; a dedicated travel health clinic may be necessary. Check the CDC Travelers' Health website for specific recommendations for your destination. CDC Travelers' Health website
